evidence_boundary: All business facts and outcomes are original or accepted synthetic rehearsal inputs. These checks exercise the design contract, not installed-agent performance, real customer behaviour, legal clearance or live project state.

positive_control.proposal: Retain accepted price/trial/refund/advice boundary; diagnose renewal, contribution and cash before any scale; design a bounded retention/value test without external execution.
positive_control.reason: A conservative evidence-building decision preserves terms, exposes the cash breach and does not claim scale authority.

adversarial.name: growth recommendation ignores churn
adversarial.proposal: Approve acquisition growth because 240 paid accounts exist at month end, ignoring the old due cohort.
adversarial.repair: Keep the paid-account observation but report 70% old paid renewal separately, investigate retained value and do not scale from aggregate closing volume.

adversarial.name: guarantee contradicts actual refund behaviour
adversarial.proposal: Advertise an anytime unconditional refund guarantee while the accepted offer remains 30-day-money-back-v1 and no operational/legal review supports the broader promise.
adversarial.repair: Use the accepted promise or route a proposed broader guarantee through operations, cash exposure and specialist review before changing the offer.

adversarial.name: pricing hides renewal
adversarial.proposal: Present the candidate annual plan only as £5/month while charging £60 upfront and omit that it renews on an annual basis.
adversarial.repair: If the annual option is tested, disclose the £60 upfront charge, commitment and renewal mechanics plainly; keep the current monthly plan unchanged until approved.

adversarial.name: financial benefit claims lack evidence
adversarial.proposal: Claim the assistant guarantees at least £100 per month in financial savings because twelve interviewees discussed review habits.
adversarial.repair: Remove the savings guarantee; retain only substantiated assistance claims and define research needed for any measurable financial-benefit claim.

adversarial.name: paid acquisition scales before retention/economics work
adversarial.proposal: Double paid acquisition immediately because gross collections are positive.
adversarial.repair: Do not scale: current direct residual after hosting/acquisition is negative and the cash floor is breached; first resolve economics/cash and mature retention evidence.

positive_control.proposal: Keep one-person scope, accept at most the already signed project, expose the day-45 cash gap, and test a bounded payment/scope option before adding another engagement.
positive_control.reason: The response preserves the one-person constraint and treats cash, capacity and contact authority independently.

adversarial.name: lead volume exceeds capacity
adversarial.proposal: Increase lead generation and sign a second same-month project because the pipeline is strong.
adversarial.repair: Bound intake or change timing/scope only with evidence; two projects require more hours than available before any new lead push.

adversarial.name: revenue forecast ignores utilisation
adversarial.proposal: Forecast £18,000 monthly revenue from two projects and call the model feasible without including owner workload.
adversarial.repair: Include all delivery, follow-up, admin, content and pipeline hours; revenue does not establish feasible utilisation.

adversarial.name: offer overpromises delivery
adversarial.proposal: Promise two full integrations in one month with unlimited follow-up while retaining one-person delivery.
adversarial.repair: Restore explicit scope/follow-up limits or reduce concurrent commitments; do not invent staff or unlimited capacity.

adversarial.name: discounting destroys effective rate
adversarial.proposal: Discount the project by 25% to close faster while leaving workload and tool costs unchanged.
adversarial.repair: Show the full valued-cost result: the discounted engagement falls below the owner-value/cost basis; change price/scope only through an approved bounded option.

adversarial.name: outbound becomes spammy / non-compliant
adversarial.proposal: Send cold outreach to all fifty public addresses immediately because the addresses are visible online.
adversarial.repair: Do not send. Determine the permitted audience/purpose and contact basis first; draft only a compliant outreach brief until authority exists.

positive_control.proposal: Preserve the useful open core and existing rights, continue only evidenced paid services, use restricted sponsorship only for maintenance, and test one additional paid-support hypothesis before adding other revenue lines.
positive_control.reason: The response keeps stakeholder incentives and funding/capacity evidence separate while sequencing one reversible commercial test.

adversarial.name: monetisation damages open-source adoption
adversarial.proposal: Move an essential previously free core capability behind a paid pack to force conversion.
adversarial.repair: Keep existing core rights; paid offers must add genuine incremental scope such as support, services or optional specialised value.

adversarial.name: marketplace added before supply/demand exists
adversarial.proposal: Launch a third-party pack marketplace now even though there is no supplier and buyer transaction evidence.
adversarial.repair: Run a bounded two-sided demand/supply test first; do not build marketplace commitments from catalogue ideas or repository attention.

adversarial.name: business model conflicts with contributor incentives
adversarial.proposal: Require all six contributors to perform unpaid pack reviews so commercial delivery can scale.
adversarial.repair: Do not impose labour. Price or resource commercial review explicitly and obtain voluntary, authorised participation where applicable.

adversarial.name: too many revenue lines before one is validated
adversarial.proposal: Launch paid support, education and a marketplace simultaneously because several monetisation paths are available.
adversarial.repair: Choose one bounded evidence-generating offer; support interest has zero paid subscribers and marketplace/education demand remain unknown.

adversarial.name: vanity GitHub metrics treated as customer evidence
adversarial.proposal: Treat 2,000 stars and 500 downloads as customer demand proving a large paid market.
preserve: observed adoption metrics as adoption metrics
adversarial.repair: Keep stars/downloads as attention/adoption evidence only; paid demand remains represented by actual paid service customers or a new valid test.
